name: Circumscribed Palmoplantar Hypokeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Circumscribed Palmoplantar Hypokeratosis

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, asymptomatic, erythematous, depressed plaques localized on the palms or soles
Histological evidence of sharply circumscribed hypokeratosis with normal underlying epidermis and dermis
Exclusion of other palmoplantar keratodermas, psoriasis, and porokeratosis by clinical and histological evaluation
Typically sporadic cases without familial inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions with confirmatory histopathology and exclusion of other differential diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing is not typically indicated.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of the plantar skin of foot

genetic: No known genetic mutations associated; typically sporadic
other: Histopathology showing sharply demarcated hypokeratosis with normal basal layer and dermis
Absence of parakeratosis or atypical keratinocytes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cornoid lamella on histology
Lesions often have raised hyperkeratotic border
Diffuse or focal thickening of the stratum corneum
Lesions typically hyperkeratotic rather than hypokeratotic
Histology shows parakeratosis and Munro microabscesses
Often associated with nail changes and arthritis

redFlags: Development of pain or significant tenderness
Signs of secondary infection such as purulence or increased erythema
references: Kanitakis J. Circumscribed palmoplantar hypokeratosis: a review. Dermatology. 2017;233(4):279-284.
Ackerman AB. Histologic diagnosis of inflammatory skin diseases. 3rd ed. 2005.
